message.content: ```json { "summary": "Make The Bayes Group site a prerendered static website. Vite + React + TypeScript + react-router stay. `npm run build` runs `vite build`, then an SSR build of a new src/entry-server.tsx, then scripts/prerender.mjs. The prerender step writes dist/index.html, dist/services/index.html, dist/training/index.html, dist/about/index.html, dist/contact/index.html and dist/404.html. Each file has the page's full markup in #root and its own head tags: title, one-sentence description, Open Graph tags, canonical link and favicon link. All page metadata lives in src/seo.ts. main.tsx hydrates the prerendered markup with hydrateRoot. Also add public/favicon.svg, robots.txt and sitemap.xml. Fix the review notes: How-we-work CSS, footer contents, pillar title class, scroll and focus on route change, and a consistent contact field style with consistent "Required" tags. Rewrite DEPLOYMENT.md for a static host with no SPA rewrite.", "files": [ "package.json", "index.html", "vite.config.ts", "tsconfig.json", ".gitignore", "src/seo.ts", "src/entry-server.tsx", "scripts/prerender.mjs", "src/main.tsx", "src/App.tsx", "src/lib/useDocumentTitle.ts", "src/components/Layout.tsx", "src/components/ScrollManager.tsx", "src/components/Footer.tsx", "src/pages/HomePage.tsx", "src/pages/ContactPage.tsx", "src/styles/global.css", "public/favicon.svg", "public/robots.txt", "public/sitemap.xml", "DEPLOYMENT.md" ], "steps": [ "Keep every existing export and behavior. src/App.tsx keeps exporting `AppRoutes`: the Routes with Layout and all pages, no Router inside it. All existing acceptance tests must keep passing. They render `` and expect the same titles, h1s, landmarks, header, footer, menu, training filter and contact form behavior.", "Create src/seo.ts with these named exports: - `SITE_URL = 'https://thebayesgroup.com'` and `SITE_NAME = 'The Bayes Group'`. - `PAGES`: an array in this order of `{ path, title, description }`: - '/': 'The Bayes Group | Evidence-driven AI' - '/services': 'Services | The Bayes Group' - '/training': 'Training | The Bayes Group' - '/about': 'About | The Bayes Group' - '/contact': 'Contact | The Bayes Group' - `NOT_FOUND_PAGE`: `{ path: '/404', title: 'Page not found | The Bayes Group', description }`. - `getPageMeta(path: string)`: returns the PAGES entry whose path equals `path` after stripping any query, hash and trailing slash ('/' stays '/'). Otherwise it returns NOT_FOUND_PAGE. Every description is exactly one sentence. It ends with a period, contains no other sentence-ending '. ', '! ' or '? ', and is unique per page. useDocumentTitle (or each page) takes its titles from these same entries, so document.title stays exactly as today.", "Create src/entry-server.tsx. Do not use import.meta or CSS imports in it, because Jest imports it. It has two named exports: - `render(url: string): string` returns `renderToString()`. StaticRouter comes from 'react-router-dom/server' on v6 (or 'react-router' on v7). - `buildPageHtml(template: string, url: string): string` takes the app's index.html (source or built) and returns the full page: 1. Remove any existing ``, `<meta name="description">`, og:* meta, canonical link and `<link rel="icon">` from the template. 2. Insert before `</head>`, from getPageMeta(url): `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`, `<meta property="og:title">` (= title), `<meta property="og:description">` (= description), `<meta property="og:type" content="website">`, `<meta property="og:site_name" content="The Bayes Group">`, `<link rel="canonical" href=SITE_URL + path>` and `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg">`. The canonical href is 'https://thebayesgroup.com/' for home and e.g. 'https://thebayesgroup.com/services', with no trailing slash, for the others. HTML-escape all attribute values. 3. Put render(url) inside `<div id="root"></div>`. 4. Keep everything else, including the module script tags. Because the result has exactly one title, description and icon link, it does not matter whether index.html itself contains a favicon link.", "Create scripts/prerender.mjs: 1. Import `buildPageHtml` from the SSR bundle (dist-server/entry-server.js). 2. Read dist/index.html once as the template, before overwriting it. 3. Write dist/index.html ('/'), dist/services/index.html, dist/training/index.html, dist/about/index.html and dist/contact/index.html. 4. Write dist/404.html from buildPageHtml(template, '/404'), which renders the NotFound page. 5. Remove dist-server afterwards (also list it in .gitignore). In package.json, set `"build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build && vite build --ssr src/entry-server.tsx --outDir dist-server && node scripts/prerender.mjs"`. Drop the `tsc --noEmit` part if the current build doesn't use tsc. Add no preinstall, postinstall or prepare scripts and no new framework. Keep current dependency versions.", "src/main.tsx imports the CSS and builds `<React.StrictMode><BrowserRouter><AppRoutes/></BrowserRouter></React.StrictMode>`. If #root has child elements, it calls `hydrateRoot(root, app)`; otherwise (vite dev) it uses `createRoot(root).render(app)`. The server tree and the client tree must produce identical markup, so hydration logs no mismatch errors. Do not read window, document or localStorage during render; only read them in effects.", "Create src/components/ScrollManager.tsx, used in Layout. It skips the first render (a ref flag) and then reacts to each `useLocation()` change of pathname or hash: - With a hash: `document.getElementById(hash.slice(1))?.scrollIntoView()`. Use the plain call; the offset comes from CSS `scroll-margin-top`. - Without a hash: `window.scrollTo(0, 0)`, then `document.getElementById('main')?.focus({ preventScroll: true })`. `<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>` already exists. On the first load nothing scrolls and focus is not moved. In global.css, give `[id]` targets / the service sections `scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--header-h) + 24px)` (at least 96px).", "Home 'How we work': give every class used inside that section a rule in src/styles/global.css. Every class name in the section's elements must appear as a selector there. - Phones: steps stack. - Inside `@media (min-width: 1024px)`: the step list uses `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr)` with a thin horizontal line, a `::before` pseudo-element on a section class using `--color-border`/`--color-accent`, behind the 40px numbered circles (`position: relative; z-index` on the circles). Pillar cards: the class on the pillar h3 gets its own rule: `font-family: var(--font-serif)`, navy, and margins between icon, title and text, matching the course and service card titles. Every class used inside a pillar card must have a CSS rule.", "Footer (src/components/Footer.tsx) shows only: - the Wordmark (in a home link), - the line 'AI enablement, training and custom development.' (exactly once), - `<nav aria-label="Footer">` with the links Services, Training, About, Contact, - '© 2026 The Bayes Group'. Remove the extra tagline paragraph. There is no other text outside links and the nav.", "Contact form (src/pages/ContactPage.tsx and global.css): - Every control (inputs, the select and the textarea) has the class `form-control`. - The `.form-control` rule uses `border: 1.5px solid var(--color-input-border)`. - `.form-control:focus` (or `:focus-visible`) uses `border-color: var(--color-accent-strong)` or `var(--color-accent)` plus the focus ring. - `.form-control[aria-invalid="true"]` uses `border-color: var(--color-error)`. - No other rule colors field borders red. - Only fields with an error get `aria-invalid="true"`. Company and topic never get it; on an empty submit, name, email and message do. - Each required field (Name, Email, Message; exactly the controls with the `required` attribute) has one 'Required' tag. All three tags are the same element type with the same className (e.g. `<span class="required-tag">Required</span>`), placed the same way, outside the `<label>`. The class has a CSS rule.", "Create the public files: - public/favicon.svg: a standalone SVG with xmlns and a viewBox, containing the wordmark's bell-curve path with stroke `#1F8A8A`. - public/robots.txt: 'User-agent: *', 'Allow: /' and 'Sitemap: https://thebayesgroup.com/sitemap.xml'. - public/sitemap.xml: a valid urlset (sitemaps.org namespace) with exactly five `<loc>` entries: https://thebayesgroup.com/, https://thebayesgroup.com/services, https://thebayesgroup.com/training, https://thebayesgroup.com/about and https://thebayesgroup.com/contact.", "Rewrite DEPLOYMENT.md for a static host: - `npm run build` prerenders one HTML file per page. - Upload dist/ as it is; no SPA fallback or rewrite rule is needed, because every page is its own file. - Unknown addresses get 404.html (configure it on hosts that need it, e.g. nginx `error_page 404 /404.html` with `try_files $uri $uri/ =404`). - Remove the `/* /index.html 200` _redirects rule, the `try_files ... /index.html` fallback and the 'unknown route returns index.html with 200' check. - Keep the security headers guidance. - Mention robots.txt, sitemap.xml and favicon.svg." ], "has_ui": true, "tests": "jest" } ```

```markdown # DESIGN.md: The Bayes Group marketing site (prerendered static) ## Users and goal **Users:** executives, operations leaders and technical managers at mid-size companies who are weighing outside help with AI. They arrive from referrals, search or a shared link (LinkedIn, Slack, email), often on a phone between meetings, and they are skeptical of hype. **The one job:** decide within about a minute that this firm is credible and relevant, then book a consultation. **Success feels like:** "These are serious, hands-on experts who will leave my team capable." Shared links show a real title and description, so the site looks credible before anyone clicks. Pages appear complete at once, with no blank flash. The message is sent without friction and followed by a clear confirmation. ## Primary flow 1. Land on Home (`/`). The prerendered HTML shows the h1 and the value proposition immediately. 2. Press **Book a consultation**. It is in the hero, the header (desktop) and the open Menu (phone), and it goes to `/contact`. The page scrolls to the top and focus moves to `
`. 3. Fill in **Name**, **Email** and **Message**. **Company** and **What can we help with?** are optional. 4. Press **Send message**. The site shows "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." and clears the form. **Secondary path:** Home → **Explore services** or a pillar's **Learn more** → the matching section on `/services`, scrolled below the sticky header → **Book a consultation**. Every page has the header CTA and the footer nav, so no screen is a dead end. ## Screens and states The site is static. There is no data loading and no network, so no screen has a spinner. Every page is a full HTML file that React hydrates. Long words and the email address use `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. **Page metadata.** Each file has exactly one title, one description, the og tags, a canonical link and ``. | Path | Title | Description | |---|---|---| | / | The Bayes Group \| Evidence-driven AI | Evidence-driven AI consulting, training and custom development led by two credentialed data scientists. | | /services | Services \| The Bayes Group | AI enablement, team training and custom AI development that deliver measurable results for your business. | | /training | Training \| The Bayes Group | Practical AI courses for executives, managers and technical teams, taught by working data scientists. | | /about | About \| The Bayes Group | Meet the data scientists behind The Bayes Group and the values that guide our work. | | /contact | Contact \| The Bayes Group | Book a consultation with The Bayes Group and get a reply within one business day. | | 404 | Page not found \| The Bayes Group | The page you requested could not be found on The Bayes Group website. | **Navigation states** - **First load:** no scrolling and no focus change. - **Later route change without a hash:** the window scrolls to (0,0) and focus moves to `
`. The focus outline is suppressed on main through `main:focus { outline: none }`. - **Route change with a hash:** the page scrolls to the target with `scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--header-h) + 24px)` (96px). **Header (all pages)** - Desktop shows the wordmark, the nav links and **Book a consultation**. - Phone shows the wordmark and a **Menu** button. The panel holds 4 stacked links plus a full-width CTA. It closes on a link click, on Escape and on a second press of Menu. - The current link has `aria-current="page"` and a 2px teal underline. **Home** - Sections in order: hero (navy), three pillar cards, How we work (4 steps, surface background), Why The Bayes Group (4 check points), and a CTA band on navy. **Services** - An h1 "Services" and an intro. - Three sections with ids `enablement`, `training` and `custom-development`. Each has an eyebrow, an h2, an intro, item cards and the line "Typical engagement: …" with a clock icon. **Training** - An h1, an intro, a filter bar (All, Executives, Managers, Technical teams), a count and a grid. - Default: "All" is pressed and the count reads "Showing 6 courses" (`role="status"`). - Filtered: for example, "Showing 2 courses for Managers". - Empty: "No courses for this audience yet." with **Show all courses**. - Many items: the grid wraps and cards in a row have equal height. **About** - An h1 "About", Mission, Why Bayes, two founder cards and four value cards. - Each founder card has an amber **Placeholder** tag and the italic note "Placeholder: replace with founder credentials and bio." **Contact** - An h1 "Book a consultation", an info column and a form card. - **Default:** empty fields. Name, Email and Message each show one identical "Required" tag. - **Error:** shown on blur for touched fields and for all fields on submit. Focus moves to the first invalid field. Only the invalid fields get `aria-invalid="true"` and a red border; Company and topic never do. Messages: - "Please enter your name." - "Please enter a valid email address." - "Please enter a message." - **Success:** a green banner with `role="status"` and `tabIndex=-1`, which receives focus. It reads "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." The form clears. The banner hides on the next edit. - **Loading:** none. Submit is synchronous and the button is never disabled. **Not found (dist/404.html)** - An h1 "Page not found" and the text "The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has moved." - **Back to home** (primary) and a **View services** link. ## Layout **Global** - Container: max-width 1200px, centered. Padding is 24px on phones and 40px at ≥1024px. - `html, body { overflow-x: hidden }`. SVGs use `max-width: 100%`. - Breakpoints: below 768px is phone, 768–1023px is tablet, ≥1024px is desktop. - Header: sticky, 72px, white, with a bottom border. **Phone (390px)** - One column, sections padded 64px top and bottom. - Hero: h1 at 40px, buttons full-width and stacked with a 12px gap. - Cards: 16px gap. - Filter chips wrap. - Contact: the info block sits above the form. - How we work: steps stack vertically with a 32px gap. Each step has the circle above its title, and there is no line. - Footer: stacked with a 24px gap. **Desktop (1280px)** - Sections padded 112px, on a 12-column grid with 32px gutters. - Hero: 7/5 split, with a decorative bell-curve SVG on the right. - Pillars: 3 columns. - How we work at ≥1024px: - The list is `display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4,1fr); gap: 32px; position: relative`. - A `::before` line runs at `top: 20px; left: 12.5%; right: 12.5%; height: 2px; background: var(--color-accent)` with `z-index: 0`. - The circles have `position: relative; z-index: 1` and a 0 0 0 8px ring in the section background color, so the line appears to pass behind them. - Why: 4/8 split. - Services: a sticky 4-column heading next to an 8-column grid of items in 2 columns. - Training: 3 columns. About: 2 founders and 4 values. - Contact: 5/7 split. - Footer: 3 columns (wordmark and line | nav | copyright). ## Design tokens **Approach:** plain CSS. `src/styles/theme.css` holds the tokens and `global.css` holds the classes. There are no frameworks, web fonts or dark theme. ```css :root { --color-navy: #0B1F3A; --color-white: #FFFFFF; --color-accent: #1F8A8A; /* mark, icons, favicon, step line */ --color-accent-strong: #17696A; /* buttons, links, focus, input focus border */ --color-accent-strong-hover: #115455; --color-accent-light: #5FC4C4; /* accents on navy */ --color-text: #2B3645; --color-muted: #556275; --color-muted-on-dark: #B8C4D6; --color-surface: #F4F7FA; --color-chip: #E6F2F2; --color-disabled-bg: #E6EBF1; --color-border: #DCE3EB; /* decorative card borders */ --color-input-border: #7A8699; /* all form controls, filter buttons */ --color-error: #B42318; --color-success: #146C43; --color-success-bg: #E8F5EE; --color-placeholder-tag: #8A4B00; --color-placeholder-bg: #FFF4E5; --font-serif: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, "Times New Roman", serif; --font-sans: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif; --text-display: 2.5rem; /* 40/48 → 56/64 */ --text-h1: 2.25rem; /* 36/44 → 48/56 */ --text-h2: 1.75rem; /* 28/36 → 36/44 */ --text-h3: 1.25rem; /* 20/28 → 22/30 serif */ --text-lead: 1.125rem; --text-body: 1rem; --text-small: 0.875rem; --text-eyebrow: 0.8125rem; --space-1: 4px; --space-2: 8px; --space-3: 12px; --space-4: 16px; --space-5: 24px; --space-6: 32px; --space-7: 48px; --space-8: 64px; --space-9: 80px; --space-10: 112px; --radius-sm: 6px; --radius-md: 12px; --radius-pill: 999px; --shadow-card: 0 1px 2px rgba(11,31,58,.06), 0 8px 24px rgba(11,31,58,.08); --focus-ring: 3px solid var(--color-accent-strong); --header-h: 72px; } ``` **Contrast pairs** | foreground hex | background hex | use | size (normal, large or ui) | |---|---|---|---| | #0B1F3A | #FFFFFF | headings, nav links, wordmark, form labels, secondary button label, card titles | normal | | #0B1F3A | #F4F7FA | headings, step and pillar titles on surface | normal | | #2B3645 | #FFFFFF | body text, input text | normal | | #2B3645 | #F4F7FA | body text on surface | normal | | #556275 | #FFFFFF | muted text, placeholder, Required tag, hints | normal | | #556275 | #F4F7FA | muted text on surface | normal | | #FFFFFF | bell-curve mark, favicon, icons | ui | | #1F8A8A | #F4F7FA | icons and How-we-work line on surface | ui | | #7A8699 | #FFFFFF | form control and filter borders | ui | | #17696A | #FFFFFF | focus ring, focused input border | ui | | #17696A | #F4F7FA | focus ring on surface | ui | | #FFFFFF | #0B1F3A | hero h1, CTA text, footer links, selected filter label, skip link | normal | | #B8C4D6 ## What this app is
The Bayes Group marketing site is a **static single-page web front-end** built with:

* Vite + React 18 + TypeScript
* `react-router-dom` for client-side routing
* Plain CSS using design-token custom properties (`src/styles/theme.css`)
* No backend, analytics, third-party scripts, or external CDNs
* `npm run build` creates a production bundle in `dist/` containing `index.html`, JS and CSS assets.

The site is intended to be served over HTTPS from a static-hosting platform (or a container-based web server) and to be reachable at `https://thebayesgroup.com` (or any custom domain you configure).

---

## Architecture
```
apps/
└─ bayes-group-site/
   ├─ index.html               # entry HTML (no external scripts)
   ├─ src/
   │  ├─ main.tsx              # boots React, imports CSS
   │  ├─ App.tsx               # BrowserRouter + Routes
   │  ├─ components/           # Header, Footer, Wordmark, Layout, etc.
   │  ├─ pages/                # Home, Services, Training, About, Contact, NotFound
   │  ├─ content/              # static data (site.ts, home.ts, services.ts, …)
   │  ├─ lib/                  # useDocumentTitle, contactForm, contrast
   │  ├─ theme/                # tokens.ts
   │  ├─ src/styles/theme.css     # :root custom properties (brand colors, fonts)
   │  ├─ src/styles/global.css    # reset, focus styles, layout helpers
   │  ├─ package.json
   │  ├─ vite.config.ts
   │  ├─ tsconfig.json
   │  └─ jest.config.cjs
   ├─ src/styles/theme.css
   ├─ src/styles/global.css
   ├─ package.json
   ├─ vite.config.ts
   ├─ tsconfig.json
   └─ jest.config.cjs
```

*All routing is client-side; the server (or CDN) must be configured to fallback to `index.html` for any unknown path.*  

---

## Prerequisites
| Requirement | Command / File | Explanation |
|-------------|----------------|-------------|
| Node ≥ 20 (the CI image uses `node:20-alpine`) | `node -v` | Required to run Vite, Jest and the build scripts. |
| npm ≥ 9 | `npm -v` | Package manager. |
| Git (for CI) | `git --version` | Source control. |
| Docker (optional, for container deployment) | `docker --version` | Used by the `Dockerfile` described later. |
| (optional) Cloud provider CLI – e.g. `flyctl`, `vercel`, `aws` | `flyctl version` etc. | Needed if you choose that host. |

The repository already contains:

* `package.json` with scripts `"dev": "vite"`, `"build": "vite build"`, `"test": "jest"`.
* `vite.config.ts` (generated by `npm init vite@latest`).
* `jest.config.cjs` (test environment set to **jsdom** for rendering tests).

---

## Configuration and secrets
The site does **not** require runtime secrets – all data is static.  
The only configuration that may differ per environment is the **custom domain** and **HTTPS termination** performed by the hosting platform.

If you later add environment-specific values (e.g. a contact-form endpoint), store them in the platform’s secret manager and reference them via a build-time `.env` file (Vite automatically injects variables prefixed with `VITE_`).  

**To-do:** Create a `.env.production` file (ignored by git) for any future secrets, e.g.:

```bash
# .env.production (example)
VITE_CONTACT_ENDPOINT=https://api.thebayesgroup.com/contact
```

Add `VITE_`-prefixed variables to `vite.config.ts`’s `define` section if you need them at build time.

---

## Build and test
```bash
# 1️⃣ Install dependencies
npm ci

# 2️⃣ Run unit & acceptance tests (Jest + React Testing Library)
npm test

# 3️⃣ Build the production bundle
npm run build   # → creates dist/ with index.html, assets/*.js, assets/*.css
```

All tests in `__tests__/acceptance/*.test.ts` are **pure TypeScript**; they do not hit any network. The build produces a completely static `dist/` directory ready for upload.

---

## Deploy
### 1️⃣ Production Dockerfile (recommended if you want container control)

Create `Dockerfile` at the project root (to-do marker if missing):

```dockerfile
# TODO: Add this Dockerfile to the repo
# -------------------------------------------------
# Multi-stage build using a slim node base, then nginx
# -------------------------------------------------
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production
COPY . .
RUN npm run build   # → dist/

# ------- Runtime image (non-root) -------
FROM nginx:alpine
# Create a non-root user (nginx runs as 'nginx' by default)
RUN adduser -D -u 101 -g 'www' wwwuser
COPY --from=builder /app/dist/ /usr/share/nginx/html
# Optional: custom nginx config for SPA fallback & security headers
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
USER wwwuser
EXPOSE 80
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s \
  CMD wget -qO- http://localhost/ || exit 1
# -------------------------------------------------
```

`nginx.conf` (to-do if you need SPA fallback & security headers):

```nginx
# TODO: Add nginx.conf for SPA routing & security headers
server {
  listen 80;
  server_name _;

  # Serve static files
  root /usr/share/nginx/html;
  index index.html;

  # SPA fallback — any 404 rewrites to index.html
  location / {
    try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
  }

  # Security headers
  add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'self';" always;
  add_header X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN always;
  add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always;
  add_header Referrer-Policy no-referrer always;
  add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload" always;
}
```

Build & run locally:

```bash
docker build -t bayes-site:prod .
docker run -p 8080:80 bayes-site:prod
# Verify: http://localhost:8080 → site loads, healthcheck: curl -f http://localhost:8080
```

### 2️⃣ Static-hosting alternatives (no Docker needed)

| Provider | How to deploy | TLS | CDN | Cost (first 10 GB/month) | Trade-offs |
|----------|---------------|-----|-----|--------------------------|------------|
| **Cloudflare Pages** | `git push` → automatic build (uses `npm run build`) | Free managed SSL | Built-in global edge CDN | Free tier up to 500 build minutes, $5‑20 for custom domain & higher bandwidth | Very low-maintenance, but only static assets (perfect for this site). |
| **Netlify** | Connect repo → "Deploy site" (build command `npm run build`) | Free managed SSL | Edge CDN | Free tier 100 GB bandwidth, $19 for "Pro" (unlimited builds, team features) | Form handling requires Netlify Functions (not needed now). |
| **Vercel** | `vercel` CLI (`vercel --prod`) or Git integration | Free managed SSL | Edge CDN | Free hobby (100 GB bandwidth, 125 build minutes) → $20 for Pro (edge-network insights) | Automatic SPA routing, easy `vercel` CLI. |
| **AWS S3 + CloudFront** | `aws s3 sync dist/ s3://my-bucket/` then CloudFront distribution | ACM-provided SSL | Global CDN | S3 $0.023/GB + CloudFront $0.085/GB; cheap at low traffic | More complex (IAM, bucket policy, invalidation). |
| **Google Cloud Run (static)** | Containerize with the Dockerfile above and deploy: `gcloud run deploy bayes-site --image=gcr.io/PROJECT/bayes-site:prod --port=80 --allow-unauthenticated` | Managed SSL | Cloud Run’s regional load balancer | $0.10 per vCPU-hour + request cost; usually <$5/mo for low traffic | Gives you container control but adds warm-up latency. |
| **Fly.io (Docker)** | $0 for the free tier (up to 3 apps, 160 GB outbound) → $5/mo for a dedicated VM | Managed SSL | Global edge network | Simple Docker deployment, includes a global edge network. |

**Example: Deploy to Cloudflare Pages**

1. Push the repository to GitHub.
2. In the Cloudflare dashboard, create a new Pages project linked to the repo.
3. Set **Build command** → `npm run build` and **Build output directory** → `dist`.
4. Add a **_redirects** file (to-do) for SPA fallback:

```text
/*    /index.html   200
```

5. Enable **Automatic HTTPS** (default).

---

## Security checklist
- [ ] **Upgrade react-router-dom** – CVE-2026-53666 & CVE-2026-53669. Edit `package.json`:


Run `npm install` and verify the app still builds (v7 API changes are primarily around `<Routes>` props; our code is compatible).

- [ ] **Add HTTP security headers** (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, HSTS).  
  *If you use the Dockerfile above – the `nginx.conf` snippet already adds them.*

| `Referrer-Policy` | `no-referrer` |

- [ ] **Enforce HTTPS only** – ensure the hosting platform redirects HTTP→HTTPS (Cloudflare "Always Use HTTPS", Netlify "Force HTTPS", etc.).

- [ ] **Validate CSP** – run `npx csp-evaluator` on the live site to ensure no violations.

- [ ] **Run a final security scan** – e.g. `npm audit` and `trivy` on the built image.

{"path": "DEPLOYMENT.md", "content": "# DEPLOYMENT.md

## Static deployment
`npm run build` runs `vite build`, bundles the server renderer and then prerenders one HTML file per page into `dist/`:

- `dist/index.html` (/)
- `dist/services/index.html`
- `dist/training/index.html`
- `dist/about/index.html`
- `dist/contact/index.html`
- `dist/404.html`

Upload the `dist/` folder as it is to any static host. There is no backend.

No SPA rewrite rule or fallback is needed, because every page is its own file. Do not add a `/* /index.html 200` rule (no `_redirects` entry) and no `try_files ... /index.html` fallback.

Unknown addresses get `404.html`. Configure this on hosts that need it, for example nginx:

```nginx
location / {
  try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
}
error_page 404 /404.html;
```

To check a deployment, open `/services` (200, its own title) and an unknown address such as `/no-such-page` (status 404 showing "Page not found").

## SEO files
`dist/` also contains `robots.txt` (allows everything and points to the sitemap), `sitemap.xml` (the five pages at https://thebayesgroup.com) and `favicon.svg` (linked from every page). They are copied from `public/`.

## Security headers
Set these headers on the host:

- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
- `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`
- `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` (HTTPS only)
- Serve everything over HTTPS and cache `assets/` (hashed file names) for a long time.

The remaining failure is in the UI flow check, not the site, so I reported it as a test dispute and changed no site behaviour. All 226 acceptance tests pass. I haven't re-run `validate` since, so the flow check will still fail on this step until the dispute is resolved.

- **Failing step:** step 41 of `ui_flow.json` expects the URL `/services#training`.
- **Why no site can pass it:** the checker (`tools/node/ui_check.mjs`) waits for `u.pathname.includes('/services#training')`. A URL's pathname never contains the `#` fragment, so that wait always times out.
- **The site is doing the right thing:** the step before it, `goto /services#training`, succeeds. The page is on `/services` with `#training` in the hash and the Training section shown.
- **What I did about it:** the dispute asks the planner to compare against pathname plus hash, or to use `/services` as the expected URL.
- **Code changes:** none. To check whether the trailing-slash redirect in `src/main.tsx` was the cause, I removed it. That didn't change the validate result, so I put it back exactly as it was.

The coder disputed that test is wrong because URL pathname doesn't include hash. This is a known issue: the UI flow test expects navigation to hash to update URL and waitForURL uses pathname includes step.url. Indeed step.url includes hash, causing failure. The task requires hash navigation to scroll to section and not on first load, and correct behavior is present. The test is wrong. According to instructions, we can list it as wrong_tests. Need to confirm that the app behavior satisfies requirement: check navigation-hash-render.test maybe passes? It appears UI flow is separate test not listed in acceptance result (only output shows failure in UI flow). The acceptance test suite includes many, but overall exit code 0? Actually overall exit code 0, but there is a warning from ui_flow failing? The static validation of "ui primary flow" failed, showing step 41 timeout. That's not part of acceptance tests but part of static validation (UI flow). It's a failing check but not a test. We need to see if that check is considered part of acceptance tests? It's a validation step; failing means verdict revise. But we can argue that check is wrong. According to instructions, if a test is wrong, we list in wrong_tests. This is a validation check, not a test file. However it's called "ui primary flow" check. Likely considered a test. We can mark as wrong_tests.

Thus we need to produce JSON with verdict revise? Actually if we mark as wrong test, we can still approve? The spec: "If you confirm that a failing test contradicts the task's text, list it in wrong_tests ... and never ask the coder to bend correct code to match it." So we can approve if all other requirements pass. However there is also static validation check failing (ui primary flow). It's not exactly a test but a check.

The instruction: "When you are done, reply with only a JSON object: {"verdict": "approve" or "revise", ...}". We should set verdict to approve if we consider the failing check an incorrect test. Are we allowed to approve despite failing static validation? The gate is tests or static validation. The failing check is part of static validation (check "ui primary flow"). /** @jest-environment jsdom */
```js
import * as React from 'react';
import { render, screen, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { AppRoutes } from '../src/App';

describe('REPRO: Scroll and focus handling on route changes', () => {
  test('initial load does not scroll, navigation scrolls to top and focuses main, hash navigation scrolls element', async () => {
    const g: any = globalThis as any;
    // Mock scrollTo and scrollIntoView
    g.scrollTo = jest.fn();
    (Element.prototype as any).scrollIntoView = jest.fn();

    // Render home page (initial load)
    render(
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/']}>
        <AppRoutes />
      </MemoryRouter>,
    );

    // No scrollTo called on first render
    expect(g.scrollTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    // Reset mocks for later
    g.scrollTo.mockClear();

    // Click on "Services" navigation link (full page navigation)
    const servicesLink = screen.getByRole('link', { name: /services/i });
    await userEvent.click(servicesLink);

    // Wait for Services page heading
    const servicesHeading = await screen.findByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: /services/i });
    expect(servicesHeading).toBeInTheDocument();

    // Expect scrollTo called with (0,0) (full page navigation)
    expect(g.scrollTo).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    const [x, y] = (g.scrollTo as jest.Mock).mock.calls[0];
    expect(x).toBe(0);
    expect(y).toBe(0);

    // Expect main element has focus
    const main = screen.getByRole('main');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(main);

    // Reset scrollTo mock for hash navigation test
    g.scrollTo.mockClear();
    (Element.prototype as any).scrollIntoView.mockClear();

    // Find link to services#training
    const trainingLink = screen.getAllByRole('link').find((link) => link.getAttribute('href')?.includes('#training'));
    expect(trainingLink).toBeDefined();

    await userEvent.click(trainingLink!);

    // Wait for element with id "training" to exist
    const trainingSection = await screen.findByTestId('training-section');
    // Alternatively find heading with id="training"
    // Expect scrollIntoView called for that element
    expect((Element.prototype as any).scrollIntoView).toHaveBeenCalled();

    // Ensure scrollTo not called for hash navigation
    expect(g.scrollTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

```js
/** @jest-environment jsdom */
import * as React from 'react';
import { render, screen, act } from '@testing-library/react';
import userEvent from '@testing-library/user-event';
import { MemoryRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { AppRoutes } from '../src/App';

describe('REPRO: Scroll and focus handling on route changes', () => {
  test('initial load does not scroll, navigation scrolls to top and focuses main, hash navigation scrolls element', async () => {
    const g: any = globalThis as any;
    // Mock scrollTo and scrollIntoView
    g.scrollTo = jest.fn();
    (Element.prototype as any).scrollIntoView = jest.fn();

    // Render home page (initial load)
    render(
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={['/']}>
        <AppRoutes />
      </MemoryRouter>,
    );

    // No scrollTo called on first render
    expect(g.scrollTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    // Reset mocks for later
    g.scrollTo.mockClear();

    // Click on "Services" navigation link (full page navigation)
    const servicesLink = screen.getByRole('link', { name: /services/i });
    await userEvent.click(servicesLink);

    // Wait for Services page heading
    const servicesHeading = await screen.findByRole('heading', { level: 1, name: /services/i });
    expect(servicesHeading).toBeInTheDocument();

    // Expect scrollTo called with (0,0) (full page navigation)
    expect(g.scrollTo).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    const [x, y] = (g.scrollTo as jest.Mock).mock.calls[0];
    expect(x).toBe(0);
    expect(y).toBe(0);

    // Expect main element has focus
    const main = screen.getByRole('main');
    expect(document.activeElement).toBe(main);

    // Reset scrollTo mock for hash navigation test
    g.scrollTo.mockClear();
    (Element.prototype as any).scrollIntoView.mockClear();

    // Find link to services#training
    const trainingLink = screen.getAllByRole('link').find((link) => link.getAttribute('href')?.includes('#training'));
    expect(trainingLink).toBeDefined();

    await userEvent.click(trainingLink!);

    // Wait for element with id "training" to exist
    const trainingSection = await screen.findByTestId('training-section');
    // Alternatively find heading with id="training"
    // Expect scrollIntoView called for that element
    expect((Element.prototype as any).scrollIntoView).toHaveBeenCalled();

    // Ensure scrollTo not called for hash navigation
    expect(g.scrollTo).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

I made the five fixes and checked them: the acceptance tests pass (226 of 226) and `validate` is clean. The only flag is a non-blocking medium-severity advisory on react-router 6.30.6, which can't be fixed from the app. I did not look at new screenshots, so the visual result is unchecked.

- **U1, red border on a pristine Message field:** no code change. Only fields with an error get `aria-invalid="true"`, and the red border only matches that value. The red Message border in your "filled in" screenshot is the real error from the earlier empty submit, which hasn't been corrected yet. The pristine Contact screenshot shows no red.
- **U2, h1 cramped under the header:** I moved the h1 into the left intro column of `ContactPage.tsx`. The contact grid now has 64px top padding and a 48px gap, so the h1 and the form card start at the same height.
- **U3, empty left column:** on desktop (≥1024px) `.contact-info` is `position: sticky` with `top: calc(var(--header-h) + 48px)` and `align-self: start`. The copy is unchanged.
- **U4, select text misaligned:** the select now has `padding: 0 40px 0 16px`, the same 48px height, border and font size as the text inputs, `appearance: none`, and a 16px chevron at `right 16px`. I also changed the shared `.form-control` horizontal padding from 14px to 16px, so inputs and select line up.
- **U5, services spacing on phone:** below 768px, `.service-section` padding is now 48px top and bottom. The "Typical engagement" line has a 16px top margin.

All changes are in `ContactPage.tsx` and `global.css`.
